text.en: Gurpreet lives in the plains of Punjab, Ritika in the desert of Rajasthan, Chandni on the coast of Odisha and Nayan in the mountains of Sikkim. They live in the same country, but their food, clothes, houses and festivals are very different. Why? Let us find out how the land around us shapes our lives.

India is a big country with many kinds of land. We call these landforms. There are plains, deserts, coasts and mountains. The land and the weather of a place decide what grows there, what animals live there and what people eat, wear and build. Let us visit four friends and see their lives.
Gurpreet lives in Amritsar, in the plains. Plains are wide flat lands, usually with rivers, so the soil is good for farming. Because there is plenty of water and fertile soil, farmers grow wheat, mustard and many vegetables. Gurpreet’s family eats makki di roti with sarson da saag and drinks cool lassi. In the Golden Temple, a free kitchen called a langar serves meals to thousands of people every day, and everyone sits together to eat.
Ritika lives in the Rajasthan desert. A desert is a dry land that gets very little rain and has sandy soil, so very few plants can grow. Plants such as cactus, khejri and babool can live there because they need little water. The camel is called the ship of the desert, because it can walk long distances on sand and go many days without water. The houses are made of mud and thick walls that keep the heat out, and water is stored in underground tanks called tankas. People wear bright bandhini clothes, play instruments like the khartal and sarangi, and eat dal-bati-churma and ker sangri, which are made from dry things that stay good in the desert. Jaisalmer has a famous fort built of golden stone.
Chandni lives in Puri, on the coast. A coast is the land next to the sea. Many people there are fishermen. They catch fish and sell them, and they know the sea very well. On the beach, artists make sand art, and children collect shells like the shankh. Chandni eats rice with dalma, pakhala and sweets like chhena poda and rasagola. The famous Jagannath Temple has the grand Rath Yatra festival, when huge chariots are pulled through the street. Coasts get strong storms called cyclones. Odisha now gives early warnings so that people can move to safe shelters in time.
Nayan lives in Gangtok, Sikkim, among the Himalayan mountains. Mountains are very high lands, and it is cold there. The mountain Kangchenjunga is very famous. There are forests of oak, pine, walnut and chestnut, and animals like the yak, whose thick hair keeps it warm. Nayan eats warm food like thukpa and sel roti, and wears warm clothes. Houses are made of wood with slanting roofs, so that rain and snow slide off. Heavy rain on the slopes can cause landslides, when soil and rocks slide down the hill. People celebrate festivals like Loosong and Namsoong, and dance and sing with traditional instruments.
Plains give farms and rivers, deserts give sand and dry plants, coasts give sea and fish, and mountains give forests and snow. People use what is near them. In plains they grow crops, on the coast they fish, in deserts they store water, and in mountains they build wooden slanting roofs. Different lands give different food, clothes, homes, work and festivals, and each way of living is wonderful. Draw your own landform and tell how people there would live. Whatever the land, people are alike in many ways. We all need food, water, a home, friends and festivals.

problem.en: Why do houses in Sikkim have slanting roofs while desert houses have thick mud walls?

text.en: Think about the weather. Sikkim has heavy rain and snow.
Slanting roofs let rain and snow slide off, so the roof does not become heavy or leak.
The desert is very hot, so thick mud walls keep the inside cool.

why.en: So each house suits its land.

problem.en: Why do fishing families live mostly on the coast?

text.en: The coast is next to the sea, where fish live.

why.en: Food and work come from the nearby land and water.

text.en: So people there learn to fish and sell fish.

why.en: They use what is near them.

text.en: That is why coastal families are often fishermen.

prompt.en: Explain how the place we live in changes our food, clothes and houses.

requiredIdeas.en: Plains, deserts, coasts and mountains are different landforms
The weather and land decide what grows and what animals live there
People eat, dress and build according to their land
Each place has its own festivals and ways, and all are special

commonMisconceptions.en: All people in India eat the same food
Houses are the same in every place

points.en: Plains, deserts, coasts and mountains are different landforms.
The land and weather decide food, clothes, houses and work.
Plains have farms, deserts have camels and tankas, coasts have fishing and cyclone warnings, mountains have yaks and wooden slanting roofs.
Every place has its own festivals, and all ways of life are valuable.
We are alike in needing food, water, homes and friends.
